items.title: The name
items.text: Owned through Atari Interactive, Inc. by Atari SA, listed on Euronext Growth Paris. FY2026 revenue was €56.0M: €46.1M from games, €7.3M from hardware and €2.5M from licensing.[^21]

items.title: The console
items.text: Atari SA sells a cartridge console called the 2600+, including a Pac-Man edition made with Bandai Namco in FY2026.[^21] The original had sold more than 20 million units by 1986.[^9]

items.title: The buried cartridges
items.text: About 1,300 games were recovered from the Alamogordo landfill in 2014. The city sold 881 of them on eBay for about $108,000, gave 100 to the documentary crew and 23 to museums.[^23]

items.title: Atari Corporation
items.text: Jack Tramiel’s company merged into the disk-drive maker JTS in July 1996 with 31 employees. JTS sold the Atari assets nineteen months later.[^11][^13]

items.title: Atari, Inc. (the second one)
items.text: The former GT Interactive, renamed in 2003, was bought out by its French parent at $1.68 a share in 2008 and filed for Chapter 11 in January 2013. A plan was approved that December.[^16][^17][^18][^19]

items.title: The programmers
items.text: Activision, founded by the four who left in 1979, was acquired by Microsoft in a transaction valued at $68.7 billion when it was announced in January 2022.[^26][^28]

blocks.title: Who has owned the Atari name
blocks.subtitle: Six owners in 54 years. The price fell by 98% between the second sale and the fourth.

nodes.what: Founded by Nolan Bushnell. Pong, then home Pong.[^1][^29]
Buys the company and funds the Video Computer System.[^1][^6]
Buys the home computer and video game business. Warner keeps the coin-operated division.[^7]
A disk-drive maker absorbs Atari Corporation in a stock merger.[^12][^13]
Buys the Atari games, trademarks and licenses from JTS.[^13]
Buys Hasbro Interactive and renames its U.S. arm Atari, Inc. in 2003.[^14][^16]
Atari Inc. and Atari Interactive file for bankruptcy protection in New York.[^18]
The former Infogrames, led by Wade Rosen, publishes retro games and sells new cartridge consoles.[^20][^21]

blocks.source: The New York Times[^1][^6][^7][^12][^14], JTS Corporation Form 8-K[^13], Atari, Inc. filings[^16], the 2013 press release[^18] and Atari SA’s FY2026 results[^21]. The 98% fall is derived: ($240M − $5M) ÷ $240M. The 1984 and 1998 sales did not cover exactly the same assets.
